item.description: DigitalCommons@UTEP (The University of Texas at El Paso) — As data increasingly shapes participation in society, there is growing emphasis on preparing youth to engage with data through computer science education. This study tests whether refining a historical landslide inventory with Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) improves machine-learning susceptibility mapping in Mandi district. Existing methods typically leverage remote sensing imagery and deep learning techniques to automatically identify unauthorized construction, or retrieve clues of ecological environmental damage from textual information such as public complaints and official circulars. item.description: Environmental Innovation and Societal Transitions — In the current context of insufficient climate action and unmet demands for climate justice, civil society organizations are increasingly turning to the courts as part of a broader repertoire of strategies to accelerate ecological transitions and drive systemic change. item.title: A machine learning-driven adaptive adjustment framework for real-time cybersickness mitigation in virtual reality
item.description: Virtual Reality — Cybersickness remains one of the most persistent barriers to the widespread adoption of Virtual reality (VR), often causing nausea, dizziness, and visual discomfort that limit user engagement. This study proposes a machine learning-based adaptive adjustment framework that predicts and mitigates cybersickness in real time using only non-intrusive head-tracking data (HTD). item.description: Geohazards & Remediation — Abstract Mass-movement disasters, including landslides, avalanches, and mudslides, are among the most critical types of geohazards influenced by climate variability and socio-economic exposure. A comprehensive global assessment linking long-term climate trends to mass-movement disasters and their socio-economic impacts remains limited, despite growing evidence of climate-driven intensification of geohazard frequency. item.description: Scientific Data — Transient populations—such as tourists, seasonal workers, and business travelers—are particularly vulnerable during hurricanes because they often lack familiarity with hazards, evacuation routes, communication channels, and social support networks. Despite their growing presence in disaster-prone regions such as Florida, their mobility behavior remains poorly documented due to limited fine-grained data. item.description: Journal of the European Meteorological Society. — Southern Europe is experiencing a shift towards a new wildfire regime, characterised by larger and more intense fires, and an extension of the fire season beyond the traditional summer months. item.description: Local Environment — Rapid and unplanned urbanisation substantially threatens resilient urban planning. It has exacerbated various environmental and urban challenges. Urban parks play a key role in supporting climate-resilient cities and overall sustainable development, enhancing the quality of life and wellbeing of urban communities. However, urban parks are often associated with crime-related activities, and the fear of crime can affect their usage. item.description: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers — ABSTRACT In this paper, I propose a novel framework—‘affordabilities’, combining affordability, mobilities and affordances—to analyse the contingent construction of affordable lifestyles through interactions between relative inequalities and spatial relations. item.description: African Transport Studies — Accra's repeated urban flooding has been predominantly attributed to rainfall variability and inadequate drainage; however, the structural role of transport infrastructure influencing flood exposure remains empirically underexplored. item.description: Computer Science Review — Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in civilian and military missions, yet their operation in denied environments is severely challenged by radio-frequency (RF) jamming that disrupts Global Positioning System (GPS) and communication links. This survey presents an adversary-centric review of UAV path planning under jamming, examining how threat-model assumptions influence algorithm design across single-UAV and swarm systems. item.description: Journal of Global Social Transformation — This Qualitative study examines how boys from the Changer Gypsy community in Lahore, Pakistan, understand and negotiate the relationship between waste collection and formal schooling. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 14 boys approximately 8-15 years of age and a separate contextual interview with a community leader (L1), the study explores children’s economic contributions, perceptions of schooling, occupational identities, household responsibilities, and future aspirations. item.title: Interconnections of climate change, water scarcity, and conflict in shaping food security in the twenty-first century: a systematic review
item.description: Agriculture & Food Security — Food security in the twenty-first century is a complex challenge shaped by environmental, economic, social, and political factors beyond mere caloric availability. These challenges are particularly critical during political conflicts and emergencies, where disruptions to agricultural production, water systems, and food supply chains can intensify food insecurity. item.description: npj Climate Action — Abstract Extreme urban heat, amplified by the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect, is a structural and recurring risk embedded within contemporary urban systems. item.description: Scientific Reports — Climate change and rapid urbanization intensify flood risk in urban agglomerations. item.title: Adaptive visual perception and navigation framework for safe indoor mobility of visually impaired users
item.description: Scientific Reports — Indoor mobility for visually impaired people is an essential problem due to dynamic obstacles and inadequate real-time detection systems. Existing solutions have been found lacking in terms of robustness and adaptability. The current research develops a robust adaptive visual perception and navigation system based on obstacle detection and indoor navigation in real time. item.description: Fronteiras Journal of Social Technological and Environmental Science — Sustainable development, as a political and pedagogical project, requires a critical articulation between environmental education, health, and public policies, understood as inseparable dimensions of social and environmental justice. item.description: Agricultural Water Management — This study examines the relationships between selected natural and anthropogenic factors and agricultural productivity in 18 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. item.description: Journal of Urban Health — Gun violence is a pervasive yet understudied neighborhood stressor that may shape chronic disease risk via inflammatory pathways. This study examined whether residential exposure to deadly neighborhood gun violence in adolescence is associated with asthma incidence, hospitalization, and functional limitation in early adulthood. item.title: Valorisation of Bos-indicus excreta biowaste into nanocellulose-reinforced PVA composite films for sustainable seed coating
item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Agro-livestock nano-composite film enhance bio-degradable polymeric property and seed coating technology. Nanocellulose derived from bovine excreta (BNC) offer a promising strategy for sustainable crop production and storage. In this study the optimized film was evaluated for dip seed coating i.e. mung bean (Vigna radiata). Nanocellulose-polyvinyl alcohol coated seeds showed significantly enhanced germination and seedling growth at 5% NC-PVA composite. After 6 days, root and shoot lengths reached 10.20 cm and 13.60 cm, respectively, compared with 6.95 and 9.85 cm for the H₂O control.

item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract Retired pesticide sites are an important category of contaminated land, and groundwater pollution at these sites remains a major environmental concern. item.description: DS Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics — This manuscript examines the legal and ethical implications framework for the application of Artificial Intelligence in Ugandan Centenary banks, with a case study focus on the Lango Sub-Region of Northern Uganda. item.description: Epilepsia — OBJECTIVE: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. item.description: bioRxiv (Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory) — Human papillomavirus-related (HPV+) cancers harbor a subset of tumor cells expressing certain senescence-related transcripts and reduced levels of HPV mRNAs. item.description: Island Studies Journal — The epistemologies based on the terra firma framework fall short in interpreting the relationship and transcendence of land and water concerning the river islands ( chars ). item.description: Island Studies Journal — The Chiloé Archipelago has been approached within island studies, yet its engagement with archipelagic thinking remains limited. item.description: Journal of Research on Adolescence — School closures can disrupt not only educational access but also the relational and institutional conditions through which adolescents experience school belonging. item.title: Atmospheric Borders
item.description: Area — ABSTRACT What kinds of atmospheres do borders produce? And what kinds of bordering are produced by atmospheric conditions? item.description: Insect Conservation and Diversity — Abstract Wildfires are increasing in severity, frequency and extent across many biomes. item.title: From Environmental Exposure to Compound Vulnerability: Reframing Public Health Governance in Environmental Planning
item.description: Research Square — Abstract The effects of environmental determinants of public health have been investigated by individual pathways of exposure, including air pollution, unsafe water, climate stress, or waste exposure. This review discusses these risks in the light of the concept of compound vulnerabilities, which sees environmental health burdens as being not only determined by exposure, but also by governance, infrastructure, planning, social inequality and adaptive capacity. The study was carried out using a systematic review following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis.
